States not listed: apply the general reasonableness test and check current law.

column2: FTC Non-Compete Clause Rule, 16 CFR part 910
column5: NOT IN FORCE. Set aside nationwide by Ryan, LLC v. FTC (N.D. Tex. Aug 2024); FTC voted 2025-09-05 to dismiss its appeals and accede to vacatur; part 910 removed from the CFR effective 2026-02-12 (91 FR 6507). FTC still brings case-by-case Section 5 actions.

column4: any contract, wherever and whenever signed (16600.5)
column5: Employment non-competes VOID however narrow; unlawful to include one or to try to enforce one; 16600.1 required notice by 2024-02-14 to current and post-2022-01-01 former employees that such clauses are void; 16600.5 private right of action with fees.
column7: sale of business (16601), dissolution of partnership/LLC (16602, 16602.5)

column2: Bus. & Prof. Code 16608 + Labor Code 926 (AB 692, 2025) - stay-or-pay
column5: Unlawful to include or require a term making a worker repay a debt, or pay a penalty/fee/cost, if employment ends (training repayment, quit fees, replacement costs, sign-on clawbacks). Such term is void (16608(c)). Worker remedy: greater of actual damages or $5,000 per worker, plus injunction and attorney fees (Lab. Code 926(c)).
column7: government loan repayment/forgiveness; transferable-credential tuition (separate agreement, not a condition of employment, amount stated up front and capped at cost, prorated, no repayment if fired other than for misconduct); approved apprenticeships; discretionary/unearned payment at outset of employment only if separate agreement, 5 business days to consult a lawyer, retention period max 2 years, prorated and interest-free, worker may defer payment to end of period, and repayment only on voluntary quit or termination for misconduct; residential property leases/loans

column3: employees incl. independent contractors (anyone not on W-2)
column5: Non-competes VOID. A worker who primarily lives and works in MN cannot be made to litigate/arbitrate elsewhere or under another state's law (voidable). Court may award fees.
column7: sale of business, dissolution; NDAs, trade-secret and non-solicit clauses are not non-competes

column5: Restraints on a lawful profession, trade or business are void.
column7: seller of goodwill; partners/members/shareholders on dissolution, reasonable area and time

column5: Former employee may compete; may be barred only from directly soliciting established customers. Conflicting terms void. A federal court enforced an out-of-state forum clause over OK policy (Oct 2025).

column3: any person paid for skilled or unskilled labor
column4: contracts entered on or after 2025-07-01; earlier contracts unaffected
column5: Non-competes VOID. Physician non-competes void (other terms survive); physician may tell rare-disorder patients where they now practice.
column6: training/relocation repayment caps: <2 yrs service 100%; 2-<3 yrs 66%; 3-<4 yrs 33%
column7: sale of a business or its assets; protection of trade secrets (to that extent); recovery of relocation/education/training expense on the schedule; executive and management personnel and officers and employees who are professional staff to them

column3: low-wage employees and health care professionals; subsection C reaches all employees
column4: 2025 amendment: from 2025-07-01; subsection C: from 2026-07-01 (Virginia default effective date)
column5: No employer may enter into, enforce or threaten to enforce a non-compete with a low-wage employee. Since 2025-07-01 'low-wage employee' includes ANY employee entitled to FLSA overtime (non-exempt), regardless of earnings, plus anyone whose average weekly earnings are below the Commonwealth average weekly wage. From 2026-07-01 (subsection C): no non-compete is enforceable against an employee discharged without cause unless the employer provides severance or other monetary payment, disclosed when the covenant is signed.
column6: civil penalty $10,000 per violation; court may void, award lost pay, liquidated damages, fees
column7: employees paid predominantly by commissions/incentives/bonuses are not 'low-wage'; discharge for cause (subsection C)

column5: Non-compete void unless annualized earnings exceed the threshold; durations over 18 months presumed unreasonable; layoff requires base-salary garden pay.
column7: sale of business, franchise, NDAs, trade secrets, non-solicits

column4: ALL non-competes, regardless of when signed; proceedings commenced on or after 2027-06-30
column5: All non-competes void and unenforceable; violation to enforce, threaten, represent that one applies, or enter into one. Employers must make reasonable efforts to give written notice by 2027-10-01 to current and former employees/contractors whose covenant is still running that it is void. 'Non-compete' now includes no-accept/no-service-of-customer clauses and any clause forcing repayment or forfeiture because the person competes. Non-solicits allowed only for customers the worker directly developed, max 18 months.
column6: effective 2027-06-30; notice by 2027-10-01; greater of actual damages or $5,000 + fees; non-solicit max 18 months
column7: sale/purchase of goodwill or of an ownership interest of 1% or more; compliant franchise sales; NDAs; trade secrets; education-expense repayment expiring within 18 months of start, prorated, released on good-cause quit

column3: physicians; also dentists, licensed nurses (RN/LVN), physician assistants (15.501)
column4: covenants entered into or renewed on or after 2025-09-01
column5: Health-care non-compete must: allow buyout at no more than the practitioner's total annual salary and wages at termination; expire within 1 year of termination; reach no more than a 5-mile radius from where the practitioner primarily practiced; be clearly and conspicuously in writing; give access to patient lists. Void if the physician is involuntarily discharged without good cause.
column7: managing or directing medical services in an administrative capacity

column3: 'covered employees' earning or expected to earn salary > twice the annual mean wage of the county of the employer's principal place of business (employee's county if employer is outside FL); excludes health care practitioners
column5: Covered non-compete up to 4 years (garden leave up to 4 years) is enforceable if the employee got the agreement at least 7 days before the offer expired, was advised in writing of the right to counsel, and acknowledged in writing receiving confidential information/customer relationships. Court MUST preliminarily enjoin a covered employee; dissolved only on clear and convincing evidence. Non-covered agreements stay under 542.335 (employee non-competes over 2 years presumed unreasonable, 6 months or less presumed reasonable).
column6: <= 4 years; 7 days; salary > 2x county annual mean wage
column7: health care practitioners (s. 456.001); non-qualifying agreements fall back to 542.335

column5: Non-competes void for employees with annualized compensation under $70,000 (wages, salary, commissions, nondiscretionary bonuses; not indexed). Restrictive covenants presumed reasonable at <= 2 years (employees), <= 3 years (franchise/distribution), longer of 5 years or payout period (sale of business); courts may blue-pencil.
